title: Your 2FA app code is never sent to you
description: Authenticator app codes aren't delivered by the website. Your phone calculates them from a shared secret and the clock. Here's how that works.

scenes.say: The six digit code in your authenticator app is never sent to you. Your phone works it out by itself.

steps: Site shows a QR code once
App saves the secret key inside
scenes.say: At setup, the site shows a QR code. Hidden inside is a secret key, which your app saves. After that, it needs no internet at all.

Every thirty seconds, your phone mixes that secret with the current time, using a cryptographic function, and keeps six digits. The website does the same sum and checks they match. It's an open standard, called R F C six two three eight.
Because time keeps moving, a stolen code goes stale quickly.
Authenticator apps beat text messages, which can be hijacked by SIM swap fraud. But either is far better than a password alone. Switch it on, and follow for more.
